items.title: Live: PM announces Fair Work Court, defends tax changes at ALP national conference
items.description: Speaking at the ALP national conference, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese says the federal government will create a Fair Work Court. Follow live.

items.title: Labor debates future, Liberals hold up pamphlet
items.description: Australia's two major parties are deliberating their futures this week with Labor's national conference and the Liberal Party's glossy new pamphlet.

items.title: The former cocaine-dealing Sydney socialite linked to a far-right news site
items.description: A "right of centre" website claiming to be news, with more than 42,000 Facebook followers, may not be as independent as it says. An ABC NEWS Verify investigation has found the site uses AI and a fake news editor.

items.title: Children in state care being lured into 'trap houses'
items.description: The ABC has spoken with experts, advocates and residential care workers as part of a 19-month investigation into the sexual exploitation of children in state care.

items.title: Jews targeted by antisemitism regardless of views on Israel, inquiry told
items.description: A recent wave of antisemitism has been far-reaching, even targeting Jewish people who are critical of the Israeli government, a royal commission probing the phenomenon has heard.

items.title: Man fined for wearing swastika T-shirt outside antisemitism inquiry
items.description: A man who wore a T-shirt with a banned Nazi symbol outside the antisemitism royal commission in Sydney has been convicted and fined $1,500.

items.title: Why highly advanced rogue AI has experts scared
items.description: An experimental AI broke out of its containment and hacked a company. Why has this got experts worried?

items.title: Unemployment rate steady for now, but could increase in coming months
items.description: The unemployment rate was steady in June at 4.4 per cent but underemployment has risen.

items.title: Researcher shocked as orca blows up a sunfish in front of her
items.description: Underwater video captures the moment killer whales in the Gulf of California slam into a sunfish, causing it to explode. Researchers say the orcas may use the technique to make it easier for juvenile killer whales to feed or they do it as a fun group bonding exercise.

items.title: Judge rejects Woodside's attempt to uncover stink-bomb protest organisers
items.description: Energy giant Woodside fails in its Supreme Court bid to force climate activists to hand over documents about the planning of a stink-bomb protest which prompted the evacuation of its Perth headquarters.

items.title: Breaking: ACT Education Minister Yvette Berry resigns from cabinet
items.description: ACT Education Minister Yvette Berry resigns after the Integrity Commission made "serious corrupt conduct" findings against two senior public servants in her portfolio.

items.title: Mamdani says he cannot arrest Netanyahu in New York but US government can
items.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani concedes he cannot order the arrest of Benjamin Netanyahu and calls on the US government to take action, but a former international prosecutor warns it could be complicated.

items.title: Melbourne football team to play without audience after sexist fan conduct
items.description: The Preston Lions, associated with the Macedonian Australian community, will be forced to play without spectators after some of its fans displayed offensive banners at a game last weekend.

items.title: Countdown clock unveiled for Brisbane 2032 Olympics
items.description: The Brisbane City Council has installed a countdown clock to mark the milestone, while an iconic Kangaroo mascot has returned in Moreton Bay.

items.title: Reading has many benefits, here’s how to fit it in to a busy life
items.description: More than half of us want to read more. Here's how to find your gateway genre and make that happen.

items.title: The intriguing film that casts the 'superior' Jude Law as the insidious Putin
items.description: Cannes darling Oliver Assayas tackles the shadowy forces of our time in his latest film, The Wizard of the Kremlin.

items.title: Nintendo raised prices due to US tariffs. Now, it doesn't want to pass on refunds
items.description: Nintendo has argued it has no duty to pass its refunds onto US consumers. It's the latest in a lengthy tariff fight.

items.title: Record $60k fine for man behind 'brazen' dump site that will cost $1m to clean
items.description: The owner of one of Victoria's worst illegal dump sites has been handed a record fine of $60,000 and ordered to pay an expected $1 million to clean up the polluted property in Melbourne's outer north-east.

items.title: Family takes racing club to court over 'enormous' hidden rubbish dump
items.description: A family discovered a large waste dump, allegedly created by a South Australian horse racing club, as they began foundation work on their home, court documents allege.

items.title: Live: Financial markets bet on rate rise in August after strong jobs results
items.description: The unemployment rate remains steady at 4.4 per cent, but a rate rise in August could be on the cards. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Japanese PM's sleep revelation sparks concern
items.description: It's unlikely Sanae Takaichi intended to start a national conversation when she tweeted about how much rest she gets. A sleep expert says her schedule would be exacting a heavy toll.

items.title: Right-wing conference arrives in UK to snoring, empty seats and bad reviews
items.description: In 10 years at the ABC, I've had some strange experiences. I can now add last week's CPAC conference in London to the list, and it's going somewhere near the top, says Riley Stuart in London.

items.title: From Mumbai to New York, young Indians gather in unprecedented movement
items.description: A student who started a youth uprising across India is fast becoming the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 12-year reign.

items.title: Tongan women 'auctioned off' for marriage in China
items.description: The ABC has spoken to multiple Tongan women who have been lured into an arranged marriage syndicate operating in China, with allegations of passports being confiscated and tens of thousands of dollars changing hands.

items.title: 'Nervous' investors retreat from housing market as downturn broadens
items.description: Australia's property market has entered a downturn after both house and unit prices fell for the first time in more than three years, bringing an end to the recent housing boom.
